subject: MSA + Order Form — allocation of regulatory fines & third-party claim handling
body:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmecloud.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acmecloud.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: ACME redlines to MSA & Order Form — regulatory fines and 3rd party claims

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the execs want to move quickly. Attaching our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (ACME_Redline_MSA.pdf; OrderForm_v3_redline.docx).

Two priority points from legal/procurement:
- Regulatory fines/penalties (GDPR/CCPA/PCI): ACME is asking that statutory fines and penalties imposed by regulators as a result of Redwood's non-compliance be excluded from the contract cap (i.e., uncapped liability) and covered by Redwood by way of indemnity.
- Third-party claims: ACME requests Redwood to indemnify ACME for third-party claims arising from Redwood's processing of customer data, including regulator-initiated claims where applicable.

We are sympathetic to keeping a commercial cap for ordinary breaches, but these two carve-outs are deal breakers for our security/compliance group unless we get stronger assurances (and a SOC2/PCI attestation). Can you route to legal and contracts and let us know Redwood's position?

We'd like to get to a call next week with legal and procurement to close this quickly.

Thanks,
Emily
_____________________
Emily Carter
Head of Procurement — Acme Cloud
emily.carter@acmecloud.com

Subject: Re: ACME redlines to MSA & Order Form — regulatory fines and 3rd party claims

Emily — appreciate the fast turnaround and the heads up on ACME's priorities. Looping in our legal and contracts team (Laura and Rishi) and Monica from AE.

Quick commercial note from our side: Redwood's standard approach to liability caps has been to use a multiple of fees (typically 1–3x annual fees depending on deal size) with narrow carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity. Uncapped liability for regulator fines is a significant departure for us and would need executive sign-off.

Requests for LGL/Contracts:
- Can you propose language that ACME would accept for a limited carve-out (e.g., uncapped for willful misconduct but otherwise caps apply)?
- Are you insisting on unlimited liability for all regulatory fines or only those arising from Redwood's direct acts/omissions?

Laura/Rishi — can you review ACME's redline and suggest defensible negotiation positions and specific redline text I can send back? Also note ACME attached a SOC2 summary — they asked for PCI as well.

I'll coordinate a 30-min legal-to-legal call next week if we have a starter position to discuss.

Best,

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 2, 2026 at 09:37 AM -0700
Subject: RE: ACME redlines to MSA & Order Form — regulatory fines and 3rd party claims

Team / Emily — I reviewed ACME's redline. High level positions and risks below, followed by suggested compromise language we can propose back.

Key points:
1) Regulatory fines (GDPR/CCPA/PCI): Customers often request these to sit outside a liability cap. Our exposure can be material and, depending on the facts, uncapped liability is commercially risky. We should push for a balanced approach that ties any uncapped exposure to narrow, defined conduct (e.g., willful misconduct or gross negligence) or to amounts actually awarded/assessed and to the extent not covered by insurance.

2) Third-party claims: Indemnities are preferable for third-party claims (defend & indemnify model), but we must retain defenses such as notice, control of defense, and carve-outs for claims arising from customer's data or instructions. Reciprocal indemnity for ACME-caused claims is reasonable.

3) PCI: For card-processor fines, liability may be governed by separate card brand rules; some vendors accept specific card‑brand carve-outs but not broad uncapped liability. We should ask for scope narrowness — e.g., Redwood indemnifies due to Redwood's negligent handling of cardholder data processed by Redwood services.

Suggested compromise redline (for Section on Limitation of Liability / Exclusions):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the aggregate liability of each Party for claims arising under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim or (b) $1,000,000. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the extent that (i) a Party's liability arises from that Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (ii) statutory fines or penalties imposed by a governmental authority under Data Protection Laws to the extent caused by such Party's breach of its obligations under the Data Processing Addendum ("DPA"); or (iii) either Party's obligations under an indemnity for third-party claims arising from a Party's breach of confidentiality or infringement of intellectual property rights. In all cases where a Party seeks indemnification for regulatory fines, such indemnified Party shall (A) provide prompt written notice to the indemnifying Party, (B) permit the indemnifying Party to assume sole control of the defense and settlement of such claim, and (C) cooperate in the defense."

Comments on the language: (a) keeps a commercial cap but carves out the most egregious categories; (b) ties regulatory fines carve-out to causation under the DPA; (c) preserves Redwood's ability to control defense and to limit settlement without admitting fault.

I'll produce a tidy redline text file with the above and some alternate dollar cap options for exec review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_proposed_redline.txt

Date: Sat, Apr 3, 2026 at 10:12 AM -0700
Subject: Re: ACME redlines to MSA & Order Form — regulatory fines and 3rd party claims

Laura / Redwood team — thanks for the quick read. A few clarifications from Acme Legal:
- ACME's ask is that regulatory fines and penalties arising from Redwood's non‑compliance are fully outside the monetary cap (not limited to gross negligence). We view regulator fines as a statutory risk that should not be swept into negotiated caps because regulators can issue significant penalties irrespective of case law on damages.
- For third-party claims, ACME expects Redwood to indemnify for regulator‑initiated claims and claims from impacted individuals to the extent caused by Redwood's processing. ACME will accept Redwood controlling the defense, but only with reasonable consultants and prior approval for settlements that would impose non‑monetary obligations on ACME.
- ACME requires current SOC2 Type II and an attestation or copy of PCI compliance evidence.

We can be flexible on the monetary cap for other categories if Redwood can accept the two asks above.

Emily Carter
LegalOps — Acme Cloud
legalops@acmecloud.com

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, Apr 4, 2026 at 15:05 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME redlines to MSA & Order Form — regulatory fines and 3rd party claims

Team / Emily — attaching Redwood's proposed redline (Redwood_proposed_redline.txt) with two negotiating levers: (1) narrow the regulatory carve-out so it applies only where Redwood's breach of the DPA is the proximate cause of the fine (we define proximate cause with examples), and (2) provide a fee‑based cap for GDPR/CCPA fines equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months if the regulator awards statutory fines (i.e., limited uncapped language becomes a backstop only for gross negligence/willful misconduct).

Suggested alternative for PCI: uncapped liability only where Redwood is contractually required by card brands to reimburse fines and where Redwood's actions directly caused the card‑brand sanction. For all indemnity claims, require: (a) prompt notice, (b) Redwood right to defend with counsel of Redwood's choice, and (c) Customer cooperation.

Negotiation playbook:
- Offer: Acceptance of indemnity for third‑party claims and regulatory fines where Redwood is the direct cause; allow cap exception for gross negligence; provide SOC2 & PCI evidence.
- Concession ask: ACME accepts pre‑agreed maximum for regulatory fines tied to 12 months' fees or an agreed dollar floor; ACME accepts Redwood control of defense subject to ACME's right to participate.

Monica, please confirm whether offering the 12‑month fee cap materially changes commercial economics — if so, I'll flag for exec review.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Contracts — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

1) Share Redwood_proposed_redline.txt with Emily and ACME legal for a quick read (attached).
2) Ask our Security team to provide SOC2 Type II report and PCI attestation links.
3) Schedule a 30‑minute legal-to-legal call for Thu Apr 8 (I will propose two time slots).

Monica — flag if the proposed 12‑month fee cap changes the discount calculus; if so we should tee up executive approval before the call.

Emily — if ACME can indicate whether you will accept a fee-based cap (12 months' fees) tied to Redwood's direct causation of the regulatory action, that will materially speed us up.

Appreciate the quick collaboration.

Best,
